# Working a ticket in its own worktree

Only a session rooted in a ticket's worktree works that ticket, so no session ever switches tickets.

A session that follows an `enter:` line moves into the ticket's worktree and works only that ticket from then on.

Every line printed by `accord worktree open`, `accord new ticket --worktree`, `accord worktree push`,
`accord worktree clean` and `accord worktree check` ends with its next action (` - next: ...`), or follows a
line `next: ...` before an `enter:` or `stop:` block: do what it says. Any other exit 2: show the message and
stop.

When Pick up's `accord worktree open <id>` did not refuse with `claimed:`, push the claim with
`git push -u origin <branch>` before anything else, even when a setup command failed.

Setup commands can take minutes: run these commands with the longest timeout your tool allows.

When `git diff HEAD -- accord/config.yml` here shows your entry under `people` as added (`./ids.md` had you add it, in this run or an earlier one) and you ran `accord new ticket --worktree`, carry it to the
worktree before you stop or move into it: add the same entry to `<path>/accord/config.yml`, run
`git -C "<path>" commit -m "<subject>" -- accord/config.yml` (`<subject>` being the line `accord subject people <email>` prints) and
`git -C "<path>" push -u origin <branch>`, then remove that entry, and only that entry, from
`accord/config.yml` here, leaving every other line of the file as it is. When `<path>/accord/config.yml` already lists your email, only remove the entry here.

When `accord/config.yml` sets `commits.message`, every commit made on a ticket branch passes it, the people subject above included (it comes from `commits.subjects.people`, which `accord lint` names
when it breaks the rule): write the message to a file outside the worktree, run `accord commit check <file>`, which names the rule when the message breaks it, and commit with `git commit -F <file>`.
`accord anchor` prints the rule at the start of every stage.

This skill runs `accord worktree clean` itself only from `/accord` with no argument and from `/accord-upgrade`;
`accord worktree open` and `accord new ticket --worktree` clean the same way on their own, so a ticket done on
the default branch loses its worktree and branches at any `/accord` command. In a tool that runs accord's session-start hook, every
session start, resume or /clear runs the same clean, so a ticket merged since the last session loses its worktree,
its branches and any folder left behind with nobody typing a command; the hook ends its clean lines with
`tell the owner the lines above`, so show them to the owner in your first reply. A New request the session check
stops cleans nothing. At the dashboard its lines are shown verbatim with the dashboard's.

After the merge, `accord worktree clean` also removes the worktree and `slice/<id>/<n>` branches a slice of another repository opened, and never touches the person's own checkout of it.

## Session check

Run it before the dashboard and before every New request, in every lane, also a New request picked from the
dashboard; at Pick up and Continue on a named ticket `accord worktree open` makes the check itself.
It runs only on the change, research and existing-ticket routes, and at Pick up and Continue; the question,
brainstorm, review and queue routes and the dashboard never stop on it, so a ticket session answers, explores,
reviews and queues, and is refused only what would touch another ticket. Run `accord worktree check`.

- Exit 0: go on.
- Exit 2 with a message that starts `this session works`: this session works the ticket it names. Show the
  message. For the dashboard, go on with it, and offer only Continue on that ticket. For a New request, stop:
  write, create, claim and edit nothing, except a New request that reports a failure in a ticket that has
  reached verify: follow `./failure.md`.
- Any other exit 2: show the message. For the dashboard, go on with it; for a New request, stop, editing
  nothing.
